description: The Svelte 5 data grid over one million server-side rows through a single rowModel prop. The columnar warehouse behind it answers every request the server-side row model sends: sort, filter, global search and the advanced-filter expression, grouping one level at a time with aggregates and child counts, infinite scroll or pages, inline edits applied back as transactions with the parent subtotal refreshed, add and delete, select-all across rows the grid never loaded with a bulk edit sent as a rule, failed blocks with a Retry row, and a grand total pinned at the bottom. A request log shows each call, its range, its latency and whether the server had the sort and filter cached.
keywords: svelte data grid million rows server
svelte grid server side grouping infinite scroll
svelte grid server side editing transactions
svelte grid select all server side

faq.question: Does the grid ever hold the million rows?
faq.answer: No. The grid holds the blocks it has scrolled into, at most 24 of 100 rows per level here, plus placeholder rows for the rest. Everything else is a request: the warehouse keeps the data as typed arrays, about 22 MB, and materialises only the rows it returns.

faq.question: What happens when a cell is edited?
faq.answer: The edit goes to the server as updateRow; the model applies the saved row back as a transaction without refetching the block, the cell flashes, and the demo calls refresh({ route }) on the parent level so the group subtotal and the grand total follow.

faq.question: How can select-all cover rows that were never loaded?
faq.answer: The selection is kept as a rule, everything except these, rather than a list of ids. The header checkbox reports all, the footer counts a million, and the bulk-edit drawer sends the rule to the server's updateWhere, which resolves it against the same filter.

faq.question: Why does a sort sometimes take a second?
faq.answer: The warehouse is a real server in miniature: a sort on a new column is a pass over a million rows, cached afterwards, so the log shows one slow request and then a few milliseconds per block. Slow network and Simulate failures switches add latency and a 30 percent failure rate to show the retry path.
